root.name: Alekhine Defense: Spielmann Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 Nf6 2. Nc3 d5 3. e5 Nfd7 4. e6

overview: After 1.e4 Nf6 2.Nc3 d5 3.e5 Nfd7 White pushes 4.e6, offering a pawn to open lines towards f7 and the black king. Black can take with 4...fxe6 or 4...Nb6, and White hopes the lead in development and the weakened e6/f7 squares make up for the pawn. Evidence is thin; this is a rare sideline.

white_ideas.idea: Open the f- and e-files with e6 and play Qh5/Qg4 ideas
Develop quickly with d4, Nf3, Bd3
Target the weak e6 pawn after ...fxe6

black_ideas.idea: Take the pawn with ...fxe6 and consolidate with ...c5/...Nf6
Use the extra pawn in the endgame

typical_structures.structure: Black pawns on e6, d5 against White d4/Nc3

character.notes: White gives a pawn for rapid development and Black has to navigate tactics around e6 and f7.

gambit.notes: After 4.e6 Black can simply capture and keep the pawn; White needs a lead in development to regain it.

soundness.notes: Probably dubious for White; Black can hold the pawn with accurate play.

structure.notes: Black's d5 pawn and open f-file give a partly open centre.

level.notes: A sideline that is more about tactics than theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: Declined with 4...Nb6
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 Nf6 2. Nc3 d5 3. e5 Nfd7 4. e6 Nb6
sublines_that_differ.how: Black ignores the pawn and keeps the structure; White is then pawn-down for nothing concrete.

character.reason: White gives a pawn for lines and tempi and both kings are exposed to tactics.

gambit.reason: 4.e6 offers a pawn that Black can capture and keep, though it is not obviously refuted.

soundness.reason: Black can accept with ...fxe6 and White has no clear compensation.

structure.reason: Black's d5 pawn stands against the open e- and f-files after the exchange.

approach.reason: A sideline of the Alekhine that strong players seldom choose.

level.reason: It is dubious, so never Beginner, but the lines are short and tactical.

plans.reason: The pawn is given for quick pieces aimed at f7.
